name: Sodium smart-account session-key validation bypass draining Lumi Finance users
summary: Sodium._validateSignature authorizes the ERC-4337 executeWithSodiumAuthSession path whenever the session-key address read out of the userOp's own callData (bytes 16..36) equals the signer address read out of the userOp's own signature blob, and never checks that address against the wallet's stored session records the way the execute branch does through isSessionOwner. checkValidSodiumSignature type 0x01 takes the signer from the signature itself and resolves it through SignatureChecker, so an attacker-deployed ERC-1271 contract that returns the magic value for any digest makes signer, session key and validation all attacker-controlled. validateUserOp then unconditionally runs _payPrefund, moving the victim wallet's ETH to the EntryPoint where the attacker is the bundler beneficiary, and _approvePaymasterToken, which asks the userOp-supplied paymaster for getTokenAllowanceCast and grants exactly the allowance the attacker's own paymaster requests. The attacker set callGasLimit to 0 so every execution phase reverted out of gas while the validation-phase prefunds and ERC20 approvals persisted, then drained the approved balances with transferFrom.

loss.notes: Quantities are the exact depletion of the victim Sodium smart accounts, reconstructed from every ERC20 Transfer whose sender carries the Sodium proxy runtime and whose recipient is one of the seven attacker addresses (3383 wallets, 5790 transfers, blocks 483390113-483407358) plus the sum of EntryPoint UserOperationEvent actualGasCost across the attacker's 113 defect-executing transactions (5449 wallets, 8657 user operations, 0.152366822290852271 ETH). Inbound WETH and stablecoins from the three Uniswap V3 pools are the attacker's own swap proceeds and are excluded so nothing is double counted. LUAUSD is valued at realised proceeds: the attacker sold the entire stolen 74480.723661281941687839 LUAUSD into Curve in two transactions for 48399.605758 USDT0, an effective 0.6493678878437041 per unit, because his own selling moved LUAUSD from 0.965 to 0.547 within the hour. The stolen 65964.433640948840615208 LUA is left unvalued: DefiLlama returns an unchanged 3.1248490646990934 quote for every timestamp around the incident and no quote at all afterwards, so that figure is a stale mark rather than a price at which this block could have been sold, and the attacker never realised more than 16000 LUA onchain. The recorded USD total is therefore a floor; published reporting of about 264000 USD marks the LUA leg at that stale quote.

ageReset.description: The Sodium wallet proxy resolves its implementation with ADDRESS SLOAD, so the pointer lives in the wallet's own storage slot keyed by its address. That slot is 0x0 at block 225855008 and 0x000000000000000000000000b5bc46df04dee31d219e7664122e29eed9506b8b from the wallet's creation block 225855009 through the pre-exploit block 483353616, and the proxy runtime hash is unchanged over the same interval, so the defect-bearing implementation became active for this execution context at its creation and stayed active.

sources.note: Reviewed the Etherscan-verified Sodium source at 0xb5bc46df04dee31d219e7664122e29eed9506b8b, the call traces of the attacker's first, fifth and seventy-third transactions, every EntryPoint UserOperationEvent in blocks 483353600-483410000, the victim wallets' runtime and implementation-pointer history, and all ERC20 transfers into the seven attacker addresses. Re-anchored: the migrated row used 0x630654fb1c8914405cf81bb02f091b049f19403a152f624f7b8a00c7724c6604 at the attacker's nonce 72, but nonce 1, transaction 0x09289efa2fd7f8c81ab66fc999894842f336d5348a5789c9a889a245bfb0738f at 483353617:4, already executes the same defect 9053 seconds earlier and is the first of 113 defect-executing transactions from the same EOA; nonce 0 is only the deployment of attacker contract 0xcb11e89a583e2468511bb8944965117700dfbd27. Re-targeted: the migrated row named the implementation itself as executionAddress, but the executing contexts are the Sodium wallet proxies, so the representative target is 0x178ff0eea283f322e855c97222557b6bd0fd2c0f, the first wallet in the anchor that delegates to the verified implementation. Root cause reproduced from the anchor: the userOp for that wallet carries signature 0x01cb11e89a583e2468511bb8944965117700dfbd2700, so checkValidSodiumSignature type 0x01 resolves the signer to the attacker contract through ERC-1271, callData selector 0x28f8aa4d is executeWithSodiumAuthSession, callData bytes 16..36 hold the same attacker address as the session key, and validateUserOp returned 0. The migrated summary called it an unauthorized session key plus a paymaster approval; the approval leg is real but only appears from the attacker's nonce 72 onward, and the primitive is the self-declared session key. callGasLimit is 0 in every userOp, so the EntryPoint's innerHandleOp always reverted out of gas while the validation-phase side effects stuck. Code history: the proxy resolves its implementation through ADDRESS SLOAD; the wallet's slot 0x000000000000000000000000178ff0eea283f322e855c97222557b6bd0fd2c0f is 0x0 at 225855008 and 0xb5bc46df04dee31d219e7664122e29eed9506b8b from 225855009 to 483353616, the proxy runtime hashes to 0x5b50b88c3767222ffbb152eddb5aa6ce3af2b2d3d210574a31752a2f64c0b221 at both ends, and the implementation runtime hashes to 0xdb623ea308ecc67d39239d5c89b2e529c5969161863b7521fa8a675e3ddf8994 at its own creation block 142595379 and pre-exploit, giving 1783929429-1719390923 = 64538506 s. The wallet was created by factory 0x5eb4bcaeb78a7a765fa3f7285ee6b3e08ccb2c09 inside EntryPoint handleOps transaction 0x0d4c4af9383e81c8b897a802121dd7c9c2747c437b4939de099d15c5c861d7c3. Loss corrected from the seed row's rounded 264000 to measured victim depletion; see loss.notes for the LUA and LUAUSD valuation treatment.

limitations: The stolen 65964.433640948840615208 LUA is carried without a USD value because no realisable price for that quantity exists, so loss.usd.amount is a floor rather than the full depletion.

A second, unverified Sodium implementation 0x46516e846ccba95fefc8da6a3cbab875367e5c46 was exploited through the same failure in the same campaign and is not represented as a separate target; curve deduplication by (incidentId, failureModeId) would collapse it into this observation in any case.
